mission: Study distant physical boundaries and alternative universe futures while preserving the distinction between observed phenomena, conditional projections and speculative philosophy.

hypotheses.title: Milky Way–Andromeda encounters
hypotheses.research_question: How does the likelihood of close passage or merger change with Gaia/Hubble motion and Local Group satellite mass assumptions?
hypotheses.methodology: Review multi-body gravitational simulation assumptions, confidence ranges and model-dependence; no independent physical prediction is claimed.
hypotheses.evidence_note: A 2025 Nature Astronomy study estimated approximately a 50% probability of no Milky Way–Andromeda merger over 10 billion years under its model; this is not a universal or guaranteed outcome.
hypotheses.observable: Stellar proper motions, distances, galaxy masses and independent N-body simulation comparisons
hypotheses.unresolved: Local Group uncertainties and long-term chaotic trajectory extrapolation
hypotheses.forbidden_inference: A future Milky Way–Andromeda collision is certain or can currently be prevented.

hypotheses.title: Solar evolution and habitability horizons
hypotheses.research_question: Which physically constrained stellar, climate and habitat scenarios alter long-term habitability, with what uncertainties?
hypotheses.methodology: Compare published stellar evolution and habitability limits; explicitly separate astrophysics from hypothetical civilization engineering.
hypotheses.evidence_note: Solar brightening threatens Earth's future habitability long before the Sun's red-giant stage around five billion years from now.
hypotheses.observable: Stellar age, luminosity, composition, exoplanet dynamics and validated climate models
hypotheses.unresolved: Exact biosphere survival times, exoplanet life capacity and any future migration feasibility
hypotheses.forbidden_inference: Current technology can preserve everyone indefinitely or reliably relocate civilization.

hypotheses.title: Cosmic expansion and dark energy
hypotheses.research_question: Do future combined observations prefer a cosmological constant, evolving dark energy or another viable explanation for cosmic acceleration?
hypotheses.methodology: Track model priors, likelihoods, error budgets and independent analyses without promoting preliminary preference to established discovery.
hypotheses.evidence_note: The universe's acceleration is observed; dark energy's nature is unresolved, and DESI 2025 reported hints rather than a confirmed discovery of evolving dark energy.
hypotheses.observable: Baryon acoustic oscillations, supernovae, CMB, weak lensing and cross-survey agreement
hypotheses.unresolved: Dark-energy equation of state and resulting long-term universe fate
hypotheses.forbidden_inference: A specific final universe scenario is already proven.

hypotheses.title: Conditional thermodynamic heat death
hypotheses.research_question: Under which assumptions about continuing expansion, entropy and dark energy does an asymptotic low-free-energy state arise?
hypotheses.methodology: Analyze competing cosmological scenarios and explicitly distinguish absence of accessible free energy from cessation of physical time.
hypotheses.evidence_note: Heat death or Big Chill is one possible model-dependent outcome. It does not logically entail that spacetime's time coordinate stops.
hypotheses.observable: Cosmological expansion history, horizon physics, thermodynamics and assumptions about ultimate particle and black-hole processes
hypotheses.unresolved: Final vacuum state, cosmic horizon thermodynamics and applicable assumptions at enormous timescales
hypotheses.forbidden_inference: Heat death is an experimentally proven final state, or it literally means time has stopped.

hypotheses.title: Time's possible boundary and alternative cosmic fates
hypotheses.research_question: Can physical time have a finite future boundary, and how do Big Crunch, Big Rip and continuing expansion models differ in their temporal and causal definitions?
hypotheses.methodology: Separate formal cosmological models from observational predictions, compare assumptions and avoid claims about what happens beyond a proposed boundary.
hypotheses.evidence_note: Big Crunch, Big Rip and indefinite expansion are qualitatively different conditional scenarios; a future end of time is not established.
hypotheses.observable: Dark-energy evolution and observational checks on relevant cosmological models, where such tests exist
hypotheses.unresolved: Nature of spacetime at singularities, possible quantum-gravity completions and philosophical interpretation of time
hypotheses.forbidden_inference: AI can leave the universe, reverse entropy or continue subjective identity beyond a terminal time boundary.
